baselinePair.note: Stored 1920x1080 native capture of the settled Game root menu, scored against the stored RPCS3 frame. This pair is the historical baseline: whole frame 18.20 dB / 0.8388 SSIM. Offline scoring of this pair is deterministic, so its gate catches tooling (decoder/metric/crop) regressions.

tolerance.rationale: Two canonical capture runs are pixel-identical (PSNR Infinity, SSIM 1.0000), so run-to-run jitter contributes nothing. The budget therefore only absorbs GPU/driver shader noise and small environment drift. 0.5 dB PSNR is a 12% MSE increase, while a visible layer regression (a moved icon, a dropped label row, a shifted gradient) moves a layer score by more than 1 dB; 0.004 SSIM is likewise far above observed noise and far below a visible regression.

capture.note: Canonical capture recipe. All animation clocks are pinned, so two runs are pixel-identical. XMB_STEAM_ROOT points at an empty directory: the stored RPCS3 reference frame's Game column predates this PC's Steam library and shows the dev_flash XMBML entries only. backgroundClock and uiClock both match the reference frame's own clock, 25/10 12:32 (the background runs the traced _DayTime curve, so the time of day matters; the 10/28 10:00 pin belonged to root__original__day__1080p, a different still). The default exe is the integration build this file's named-state references were last saved from; pass --exe when the integration build moves.

stateSelfBaseline.rationale: Named states have no RPCS3 frame: their reference is the deterministic native render itself, so a fresh capture must reproduce that frame (self-baseline regression gate, not firmware fidelity). Two runs of every state are byte-identical on this machine (PSNR Infinity, SSIM 1.0000). 55 dB still catches any deterministic drawing change (one changed 255-level pixel already costs ~68 dB on a 1080p frame) while leaving room for GPU/driver shader noise; 0.9995 SSIM is the same margin. Refresh a reference deliberately after an intended rendering or layout change with --states --save-reference.

states.description: Game column root: the installed Steam titles first, inline as ICON0 tiles like installed PKGs (user direction 2026-11-02), then Steam Store, one All Games folder (detail = distinct Steam titles) and the dev_flash utilities. No top-level Not Installed row.

states.name: steam-all-games
states.description: All Games page: All Titles, then one folder per non-empty Steam collection (collection-name order), then Not Installed and Family Shared. Only the 14 folder rows are asserted, not the title lists inside them.

states.name: steam-store-sections

states.name: steam-not-installed

states.name: xmb-notification
states.description: A notification pop-up over the settled Game root, raised through Shell::notify - the same path a real event uses, not a drawing test. The plaque sits under the information bar; the sidecar reports the queued pop-up and its icon, and the log reports the enqueue.

states.name: xmb-volume-hud
states.description: The transient volume HUD at a pinned 25%, driven through the VOLSET script token (the same apply path the Windows media keys use); VOLRESTORE puts the endpoint back after the grab. The HUD has no sidecar field, so its level is asserted from the app's own read-back line, which records what Windows reported after the write.

states.name: video-options-panel
states.description: The Triangle options panel open on the Video Library folder page: the firmware row set Sort By / Open / Copy / Delete / Information in two groups (utility row above, actions below), no Close row - Circle closes - and the menu opens focused on the first action row on the measured full-height band, over the dimmed page. The panel is a composite, not a page, so its own log line and the page's sidecar rows are the state oracle.

log.pattern: shell: options opened category= video depth= 1 .*rows= 5 Sort By\|Open\|Copy\|Delete\|Information

states.name: continue-watching
states.description: Continue Watching populated from a seeded resume record: the Video column's first row opens the page built from media/resume, one row for the remembered file with its Resume at line.

log.pattern: continue watching: page opened with 1 row\(s\)

states.name: continue-watching-empty
states.description: Continue Watching with no remembered positions: the row reports the firmware's own empty state as a dialog over the Video column instead of opening an empty page.

states.name: subtitle-cue
states.description: A sidecar subtitle cue over local media paused at position 0: the fixture clip plus its own .srt, opened from the Video Library page. Pausing and then seeking left clamps to exactly 0, so the video frame, the 0:00 controls and the first cue are the same on every run. The sidecar reports the cue number, its file and the position; the log reports the sidecar discovery.

states.name: jellyfin-signin
states.description: The in-XMB Jellyfin sign-in page opened from a registered Jellyfin service row in the TV column (the seeded apps.json registration, no server contacted). Six rows (Server URL, Username, Password, Stay Signed In, Sign In, Cancel), focus on Username, the registration URL shown read-only, and the page, not a modal widget.

log.pattern: jellyfin: sign-in page opened rows= Server URL\|Username\|Password\|Stay Signed In\|Sign In\|Cancel focus= Username

states.name: steam-download-page
states.description: Download Management in the Network column, listing a fixture Steam download queue (four manifests in scanner order: active, paused, queued, pending). The page's own .dl.json dump asserts the rows, their state text and their details; the fixture root comes from the recipe's env, so the machine's real Steam queue cannot change the state.

log.pattern: steam downloads: page opened with 4 row\(s\)

states.name: music-player-page
states.description: The Music player page with the Visual Player OFF (its default): a generated silent tagged WAV from the Music Library page, paused and sought back to exactly 0, so the cover, title/artist/album, codec label, 0:00 bar and guide line are the same on every run. No bars and no glow are drawn with the visualizer off (audit/MUSIC-PLAYER.md, Visualizer).

states.name: music-visual-player-panel
states.description: The Music control panel (Triangle) with focus on the eighth cell, the Visual Player button (tex_cp_vislizer under the focus plate, the string "Visual Player" under the panel). Paused at 0 so the panel's 00:00 / 00:30 read-out is fixed.

states.name: music-visual-player-on
states.description: The Music player page with the Visual Player ON and the track playing, over a silent generated track. The spectrum is pinned (XMB_MUSICVIS_FIXED=1 feeds a fixed 40-band spectrum and loudness instead of the audio tap, so the bars, peak caps and cover glow settle to the same pixels; live audio levels are not reproducible and are not gated). The time bar and read-outs move with playback, so only the regions above the bar are scored; the frame is grabbed about 6 s after the last input, before the 8 s idle style.

states.name: photo-gallery-piles
states.description: The Photo Gallery's pile overview over the read-only 374-photo library (C:/dev/out/gal/photos): opened from the Photo column's Photo Gallery row, boot fall finished, the 7 s help card timed out (BOOT_HELP_DISP_TIME), focus settled on the first pile. The scene clock is the pinned render clock, the photo set and its EXIF dates are fixed files, and thumbnails are decoded before the grab. The gallery has no sidecar fields, so the log lines are its state oracle.

states.name: photo-gallery-grid
states.description: The Photo Gallery's grid of the first pile (two photos, 1 / 2) after Cross enters it: the focus ring on the first cell with its pulse, the header count and the bottom guide. Same fixed library and pinned clocks as photo-gallery-piles.

states.name: game-boot-logo
states.description: The console game-boot sequence held at 1.4 s of anim_gameboot (XMB_GAMEBOOT_AT pins the clock, never arms the Finished timer and never launches the title): the UI hidden, a black plane, tex_ps3logo at about full opacity. Reached the way a launch reaches it, by Enter on an imported game row (a stand-in app that is never started).

states.name: game-boot-fade-out
states.description: The game-boot sequence held at 1.68 s, inside the 174 ms fade-out: the logo scaling toward 1.28 while its alpha falls. Pins the second half of the traced timeline (Fade to 0 and Resize at 1.6 s).

states.name: auto-off-guide
states.description: The Auto-Off guide plate at the Options hint's anchor over the Game root: power/idleMinutes 11 makes the guide due from 60 s of idle (the firmware shows it for the last 600 s), and the idle token pins the shell's idle time at 70 s, so no real time passes. XMB_POWER_DRY_RUN stops the display-off request; the sidecar reports it was not made.

states.name: ingame-xmb
states.description: The in-game XMB over a captured game frame: a stand-in game window of our own (work/v2-stubgame.cpp, a plain GDI window launched by this script's own Enter on its imported row, game boot off), then a PS tap. The captured window frame is fitted and dimmed behind the columns, the Quit Game row is inserted and the guide reads Back to Game Screen. The sidecar reports titleRunning and inGame; the stub is ended afterwards by pid. The window capture goes through the compositor, so the frame is pinned for this machine's window theme, not across machines.

log.pattern: ingame: row ingame:quit inserted in game

states.name: raf-static-scene
states.description: The offscreen RAF still (--raf-render): the firmware's coldboot.raf scene drawn once, with no window and no clock, from the read-only dev_flash. The command prints its actor / model / texture / triangle counts, which are the state oracle. No XMB surface shows it yet (audit/RAF-THEMES.md: nothing is drawn behind the XMB), so this gates the renderer itself.

log.pattern: RAF still: 6 actors, 1 models, 6 textures, 18 model triangles, 1920x1080, camera=scene light=scene

states.name: settings-autologon-info
states.description: Settings > System Settings > Windows automatic sign-in, the information page Cross opens on that row (row 30 of the 34-row page): the status line and the netplwiz / Sysinternals Autologon steps. XMB_AUTOLOGON_FAKE="1|gate-user|gate-user" replaces the Winlogon read, so the status is "On for gate-user" on every PC and the registry is never read for the capture; XMB_AUTOSTART_TASK names a task that does not exist, so nothing can touch the real logon task. The page is a message page over the list, so the sidecar still says depth 1 on that row; the boot log line `autologon: on for gate-user` is the oracle that the faked state was used (audit/AUTOLOGON.md).

states.name: settings-autologon-row
states.description: The Settings > System Settings list with the Windows automatic sign-in row focused: its value column reads "On for gate-user" (XMB_AUTOLOGON_FAKE="1|gate-user|gate-user", so no registry read) and its description is under the title. Start at Sign-in above it is dimmed with no value because a dev build has no watchdog.ps1 beside the exe (a packaged build would show On/Off there). Regions leave out the About row and the clock plate: the About row carries the build version and Qt version text, which changes with every version bump.

states.name: first-run-autologon-step
states.description: The first-run wizard (--first-run on a scratch data dir) stopped on its Windows Automatic Sign-in step, with the status faked to Off (XMB_AUTOLOGON_FAKE="0|gate-user|gate-user", no registry read): the row, its value Off, the guidance for that state, Continue and Skip This Step. The script only ever presses Cross on rows it names: Set Up This System (welcome), Continue (firmware, index 1; the Download from Sony row is index 3 and is never reached), Skip This Step (library, index 5; the Use the Windows Folders row at index 0 is never pressed), Skip This Step (Controllers), Skip This Step (Start at Sign-in, index 2; its toggle row at index 0 is never pressed). Nothing is fetched, no folder or setting is written outside the scratch data dir and XMB_AUTOSTART_TASK names a task that does not exist. The step order assumes one screen (a second screen adds a Choose the Screen step before the controller step and the entryId assertion then fails); recipe field appArgs passes --first-run (audit/FIRST-RUN.md, audit/AUTOLOGON.md).

states.name: ingame-enter-text
states.description: The in-game XMB with the Enter Text row focused (ZF2): keypad icon, the row title, Quit Game above it, Software Manual and the Artwork rows below, Back to Game Screen in the guide. The stand-in game window of our own (work/v2-stubgame.cpp) is launched by this script's own Enter on its imported row, game boot off, then a PS tap opens the in-game XMB over the captured window frame (the same set-up as ingame-xmb), and 8 DOWN steps land on the Enter Text row that follows Quit Game (audit/ZF-TEXT-ENTRY.md, ZF2). The stub is ended afterwards by pid (stubLog). The window capture goes through the compositor, so the frame is pinned for this machine's window theme, not across machines. Regions start below the compositor-drawn title bar (y 140): its backdrop shifts by up to 2 levels over time on this machine (the stored ingame-xmb frame shows the same 62 dB drift over its top 75 rows), which is noise, not a drawing change.

log.pattern: ingame: row ingame:quit inserted in game

states.name: ingame-enter-text-keyboard
states.description: Cross on the Enter Text row opens the XMB's own keyboard over the in-game XMB (title Enter Text, field limit 256) and the script types the short fixed text "Gate 42" with the type= token: the field shows it, the focused key is g (the first character the keyboard cursor rests on), Prediction and Enter keys are drawn as the firmware layout. The stand-in game window of our own (work/v2-stubgame.cpp) is launched by this script's own Enter on its imported row, game boot off, then a PS tap opens the in-game XMB over the captured window frame (the same set-up as ingame-xmb), and 8 DOWN steps then Cross on the Enter Text row that follows Quit Game (audit/ZF-TEXT-ENTRY.md, ZF2). The stub is ended afterwards by pid (stubLog). The window capture goes through the compositor, so the frame is pinned for this machine's window theme, not across machines. Nothing is ever delivered: the keyboard's Enter is never pressed (the script ends with quit while the keyboard is open), the typed text is held only in the keyboard's field and is in no log line, and the only window that could receive text is the stub, which reads no text at all. Regions start below the compositor-drawn title bar (y 140): its backdrop shifts by up to 2 levels over time on this machine (the stored ingame-xmb frame shows the same 62 dB drift over its top 75 rows), which is noise, not a drawing change.
